title: Squint brings visual AI help directly onto the desktop
friendlyTitle: Draw a box on your screen and ask AI what it means
summary: Squint is a Windows and Linux desktop app that lets users draw a box around part of the screen and ask an AI about it without switching applications or uploading a screenshot manually. It supports follow-up questions and stores chat history locally, while model answers require a network connection.
friendlySummary: Squint lets you select part of your screen and get an explanation beside it. It works on Windows and Linux, with macOS planned later.
whyItMatters: The product removes enough friction to make visual assistance useful during ordinary work, from interpreting charts to choosing downloads. Sensitive screens remain a reason to pause: the selected image region is still sent to an online model for an answer.
friendlyWhyItMatters: It can save time when a chart, picture or download option is confusing. Do not select private information, because the answer comes from an online AI service.
